data.name: Caloric restriction
data.description: Reduced caloric intake without malnutrition; associated with lifespan extension across species.
data.description_beginner: Eating meaningfully fewer calories without becoming malnourished. It's linked to longer lifespan across many species and is one of the classic ways researchers dial down mTOR signaling through diet.

studies.title: Caloric restriction improves health and survival of rhesus monkeys

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Direct comparison of two long-term primate CR studies (NIA, Wisconsin) supports consistent health benefits; the survival effect depended on study design and control-diet composition.

studies.title: Safety of two-year caloric restriction in non-obese healthy individuals
studies.authors: Romashkan SV; Ravussin E et al.

evidence.label: Human study
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Two years of sustained 25% caloric restriction in healthy non-obese adults was safe overall, though it lowered bone density more than controls.

studies.title: 4E-BP extends lifespan upon dietary restriction by enhancing mitochondrial activity in Drosophila
studies.authors: Zid BM; Rogers AN; Katewa SD; Vargas MA; Kolipinski MC; Lu TA; Benzer S; Kapahi P

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Connected the dots between diet, mTOR, and lifespan. 4E-BP, an mTOR target, is upregulated on dietary restriction and here was shown to be REQUIRED for the lifespan boost, working by selectively boosting translation of mitochondrial genes. A rare case pinning a specific mTOR effector to the longevity benefit of eating less.

studies.title: Extending healthy life span--from yeast to humans
studies.authors: Fontana L; Partridge L; Longo VD

evidence.label: Review — secondary literature, not a new result
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Influential review proposing that dietary restriction and reduced nutrient-sensing signalling (mTOR, GH/IGF-1) may slow ageing through similar, evolutionarily conserved mechanisms. Lifespan extension is shown in yeast, invertebrates, rodents and rhesus monkeys; in humans the evidence is limited to protective biomarker changes and genetic associations.
